title: Sage gargle for sore and inflamed throat
subtitle: An astringent gargle for throat inflammation
excerpt: A sage infusion cooled to a comfortable temperature and used as a gargle for an inflamed, sore throat. One tablespoon of fresh sage or one teaspoon of dried, steeped in 200 ml of just-boiled water for ten minutes, then strained and cooled. Gargle for thirty seconds, three to four times a day. Not for swallowing.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), sage entry: records the gargle use of sage infusion for inflamed throat and mouth, referencing the astringent and antimicrobial properties. Culpeper, The English Physician (1652), sage entry: documents use for throat inflammations. BHP (1983) sage monograph: dosing reference and safety note on thujone. EMA HMPC monograph on Salviae officinalis folium (2016): confirms traditional use for mild mucosal inflammations of the mouth and throat, gargle route; safety guidance on thujone and pregnancy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The prepared gargle liquid keeps in a clean covered glass jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Warm to a comfortable temperature before each gargle session. Make a fresh batch each day.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in a clean covered glass jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Discard any unused liquid after one day.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation held at the back of the throat and gargled for thirty seconds, then spat out. Never swallowed at therapeutic-strength concentrations.
A herb that causes the tissues it contacts to contract and dry slightly, traditionally used to reduce inflammation and weeping in mucous membranes.

content.text: is a cooled sage infusion used directly on an inflamed, sore throat. Sage's

and antimicrobial properties are what western herbalists draw on here; making contact with the sore tissue directly is the point of a gargle over a tea. One tablespoon of fresh sage or one teaspoon of dried per 200 ml of just-boiled water, steeped covered for ten minutes, strained and cooled. Gargle thirty seconds and spit out every time. This preparation is for external use at the throat only; it is not for swallowing.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Do NOT swallow this gargle. Sage contains thujone, a volatile oil that accumulates with repeated swallowing of concentrated preparations. Gargle for thirty seconds and spit the liquid out each time. Rinsing the mouth with a small amount of water afterwards is fine.

Pregnancy: do not use sage at therapeutic dose in pregnancy. This includes using this gargle preparation. Culinary amounts of sage in cooking are not the same as a daily medicinal gargle.

Breastfeeding: sage is the traditional milk-suppressing herb and actively reduces milk supply. Do not use this gargle during established breastfeeding unless the aim is weaning.

Long-term use: do not use this gargle daily for more than one to two weeks without a break, owing to the cumulative thujone exposure even via the gargle route.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine, or a paediatric doctor, before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve. Children who cannot reliably spit out a gargle should not use a gargle preparation.

items.prepNote: fresh sage leaves, roughly chopped; or 1 tsp dried sage leaf

content.text: Put 1 tablespoon of fresh sage (or 1 teaspoon of dried) into a small teapot or covered cup.
Pour over 200 ml of just-boiled water and lid immediately.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water turns pale gold and smells clearly of sage.
Strain through a sieve into a clean glass. Allow to cool to a comfortable gargling temperature: warm but not hot enough to scald.
Take a mouthful, tilt the head back, gargle for 30 seconds, and spit out. Repeat until the cup is used up.
Gargle three to four times a day, for the duration of symptoms, up to seven days. Always spit out the gargle liquid. If the sore throat does not improve within five days, or worsens, see your doctor.
The prepared gargle keeps in a clean covered glass jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Warm to a comfortable temperature before each use. Make a fresh batch each day.
When not to use this remedy
See a doctor for a sore throat lasting more than a week. Very severe pain, difficulty swallowing or breathing, drooling, a hot lump in the neck, or a high fever.
Do not use in pregnancy, during established breastfeeding, in children who cannot reliably spit out the liquid. Or for more than seven days without medical review.

items.symptom: Gargle feels harsh or causes further irritation
items.cause: Liquid is too hot, or too concentrated
items.fix: Allow to cool more before gargling. If the infusion smells very strong, dilute with a little cooled boiled water.

items.cause: Dried sage is old or stored in the light
items.fix: Replace with fresh dried sage. It should smell clearly herbal and camphor-edged when rubbed between the fingers.
